classification.difficultyReason: The identity and selected coefficient are supplied; express all complementary index pairs symbolically, use combination symmetry and equate coefficients, transferring the established proof method.

content.prompt:
If the entries of any row are squared and added, the sum is the middle entry in the row twice as far down. We proved this in an investigation earlier, we will prove it again using a different expansion.

By comparing coefficients of $x^n$ on both sides of the identity $(1+x)^n(1+x)^n=(1+x)^{2n}$, show that
$$({}^{n}C_0)^2+({}^{n}C_1)^2+({}^{n}C_2)^2+({}^{n}C_3)^2+\cdots+({}^{n}C_n)^2={}^{2n}C_n.$$

answer.short: The coefficient of $x^n$ on the LHS is $\sum_{r=0}^{n}{}^{n}C_r\,{}^{n}C_{n-r}=\sum_{r=0}^{n}({}^{n}C_r)^2$, using ${}^{n}C_{n-r}={}^{n}C_r$. On the RHS it is ${}^{2n}C_n$. Equating these coefficients proves the identity.
answer.worked:
By the binomial theorem,
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=(1+x)^n(1+x)^n\\\mathrm{LHS}&=\bigl({}^{n}C_0+{}^{n}C_1x+{}^{n}C_2x^2+\cdots+{}^{n}C_nx^n\bigr)\times\bigl({}^{n}C_0+{}^{n}C_1x+{}^{n}C_2x^2+\cdots+{}^{n}C_nx^n\bigr).\end{align*}$$

Terms contributing to $x^n$ have powers adding to $n$. Its coefficient on the LHS is
$$\begin{aligned}&{}^{n}C_0\,{}^{n}C_n+{}^{n}C_1\,{}^{n}C_{n-1}+{}^{n}C_2\,{}^{n}C_{n-2}+\cdots+{}^{n}C_n\,{}^{n}C_0.\end{aligned}$$

Using ${}^{n}C_r={}^{n}C_{n-r}$, this coefficient is
$$({}^{n}C_0)^2+({}^{n}C_1)^2+({}^{n}C_2)^2+\cdots+({}^{n}C_n)^2.$$

Also,
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{RHS}&=(1+x)^{2n}\\\mathrm{RHS}&={}^{2n}C_0+{}^{2n}C_1x+\cdots+{}^{2n}C_nx^n+\cdots+{}^{2n}C_{2n}x^{2n}.\end{align*}$$

The coefficient of $x^n$ on the RHS is ${}^{2n}C_n$. Equating coefficients therefore gives
$$({}^{n}C_0)^2+({}^{n}C_1)^2+({}^{n}C_2)^2+\cdots+({}^{n}C_n)^2={}^{2n}C_n.$$
